title: Sheng Kee Fridays
body: Dagny’s favorite activity to celebrate Fridays is buying pastries at Sheng Kee before class. She stores her purchase data in a table, pastries, to keep track of her spending. Assume she never purchases the same item twice. Each row represents an individual purchase. The first few rows look like this:\n##figure1.gif##\n##figure2.gif

figureAlts.figure1.gif: A table of pastries with their category, price, and a satisfaction rating out of 10. Row 1: Hot Dog Bun, Savory, 2.75, 8.5; Row 2: Yudane Milk Bun, Sweet, 2.99, 9; Row 3: Summer Romance, Sweet, 2.79, 10; Row 4: Pineapple Bun, Sweet, 2.45, 7.75; Row 5: Ham and Cheese Croissant, Savory, 3.15, 7.25.
figureAlts.figure2.gif: (c) Dagny's budget is getting tight, and she wants to buy pastries that will give her the most satisfaction per dollar. Write lines of code that will help us achieve this. i. First, create an array that contains each purchase's satisfaction per dollar. Then, add a new column called "satisfaction per $", to the pastries table. A fill-in-the-blank code block follows. The first line defines score_array as pastries with a blank method and argument, divided by pastries with another blank method and argument. The second line redefines pastries by adding a new column with a blank name and a blank array.
